:::{#thm-det-product}
#### Determinant of a product

For $p \times p$ matrices $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$,

$$
\det(\matr{A}\matr{B}) = \det(\matr{A}) \det(\matr{B}).
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-det-product}
#### Checking the product rule

For $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$
and $\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
@exm-determinant gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\det(\matr{A}) &= 2 \cd 1 - 1 \cd 0 \\
&= 2
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\det(\matr{B}) &= 1 \cd 1 - 0 \cd 3 \\
&= 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

The product is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{A}\matr{B}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 3 & 2 \cd 0 + 1 \cd 1 \\ 0 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 3 & 0 \cd 0 + 1 \cd 1 \end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
\end{aligned}
$$

with

$$
\begin{aligned}
\det(\matr{A}\matr{B}) &= 5 \cd 1 - 1 \cd 3 \\
&= 2 \\
&= \det(\matr{A})\det(\matr{B}).
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-det-product-proof}
#### An example is not a proof

@exm-det-product checks @thm-det-product
for one pair of $2 \times 2$ matrices,
which shows the theorem holds there
but does not prove it for every pair.
The proof needs properties of the determinant
that these notes don't develop;
see @banerjee2014linear.

:::

::: notes
See also <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant>.
:::
